title: Idaho family sues after irrigation shutoff ruins crops on 1,000-acre farm
content: An Idaho family, whose farm thrives along the Snake River, has initiated legal action against the state regarding an emergency order that ceased their irrigation due to dwindling water levels. This abrupt halt has jeopardized their crops and could threaten their agricultural enterprise. They assert that their property rights were infringed upon without due process or fair compensation, highlighting a larger issue surrounding water rights management in the region.

title: Georgia man grew farm to 1,600 acres; $3.2bn pipeline now runs through his land

The pipeline's path was changed to avoid a utility executive's residence, which raises questions about favoritism. Southern Natural Gas initially planned to use an existing easement on Peek's land, but later deviated from that route. Peek has filed a legal challenge with federal regulators to revert to the original route.

title: Albany’s oldest house reopens after 13-year, $3m restoration
content: The Van Ostrande-Radliff House, a historical gem built in 1728, has finally emerged from decades of obscurity thanks to a meticulous restoration. Now the proud headquarters of the Historic Albany Foundation, this iconic building is committed to preserving Albany's rich architectural heritage. Visitors can explore engaging classroom spaces, a well-stocked research library, and even a parts warehouse, all while immersing themselves in the colonial history of Albany.

title: How Jensen Huang's $30M to Stanford University helped open engineering centre
content: In 2010, Jensen Huang and Lori contributed to establish the Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center at Stanford University. The center was designed for collaboration among engineering, science, and medicine students and researchers. It features laboratories, workshops, and a library to support academic pursuits and innovation. Stanford’s administration emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary work in modern engineering education. This initiative reflects a commitment to advancing future innovations and research.

title: Val Kilmer turned 5,328-acre New Mexico ranch into retreat, then sold most of it
content: In 2011, Val Kilmer’s scenic Pecos River ranch in New Mexico changed hands after years on the market. Initially listed at $33 million, the asking price dropped to $18.5 million. The ranch not only boasted abundant natural beauty and guest facilities but also held a storied connection with Hollywood. Eventually, it was acquired by Texas oil tycoon Benjamin A. Strickling III and his wife, concluding Kilmer's chapter with the property.

title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35M estate: Why is a $75,000 sewer dispute escalating?

Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, security and potential damage to a century-old shared sewer pipe, with one neighbor citing a $75,000 repair estimate. Kelce’s construction team says it has made several compromises, but some landscaping proposals remain unresolved following recent planning board discussions.

title: Global warming could make Russia richer. It could also bring Nato closer to its doorstep
content: As the Arctic warms, Russia faces both opportunities and significant challenges regarding its environment and infrastructure. The Northern Sea Route is becoming a vital transit corridor, potentially boosting Russian exports to Asian markets. However, increased traffic raises risks associated with accidents and environmental harm. Despite potential economic benefits, Russia must contend with severe infrastructure damage from permafrost thaw.

title: Elon Musk fires another salvo over Starlink delay, targets Ambani again
content: Elon Musk argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country . he said that he was the “real boss of India” and questioning why Starlink was yet to receive clearances to begin commercial operations .

title: SC: Nothing wrong in deleting dead or those who've shifted
content: supreme court said there is nothing wrong in deletion of names of the dead . those who have either shifted out from the ward or duplicate names during special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls would be used for local body polls in Andhra Pradesh . a bench of chief justice of india and justices refused to entertain YSR Congress Party's appeal against the decision .

title: SC junks challenge to TN speaker's call to accept ADMK plea to condone 21 'rebels'
content: a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when the party has condoned the lapse and withdrawn its petitions seeking their disqualification . the petitioner said that by their very conduct, the 25 MLAs, of whom four have resigned, indulge in anti-party activity . a person who is not even an MLA cannot challenge the speaker's decision .

title: Chemists, wholesalers may need govt nod to advertise prescription drugs
content: health ministry proposes to extend existing curbs on advertisements of prescription medicines . the proposal assumes significance as regulators have raised concerns over promotion of potent prescription medicines, including antibiotics, hormonal preparations, psychotropic drugs, anti-cancer medicines and life-saving injectables .

title: Judge recuses from Punjab government appeal case
content: justice sheel Nagu recused from hearing govt's appeal against the HC's order directing a CBI probe into an alleged bribe syndicate . he was chief justice of . Punjab and Haryana HC for nearly two years prior to his elevation to . Supreme Court .

title: How many trains can one stop? Can't halt youth of India: Chirag Paswan
content:
NEW DELHI: "They are the youth of India. Nobody can stop them," BJP ally and Union minister Chirag Paswan said Friday, replying to allegations that govt was curbing train and metro services to stop people from attending Saturday's protest called by CJP over the SIR issue. "Some people are trying to spread such misconceptions. How many trains can one stop? How many roads can one block? They are India's youth, capable of showing the way to the world. Generations have done it. No one can stop them," the LJP (Ram Vilas) president told reporters on the sidelines of an event. After CEC Gyanesh Kumar came under scrutiny following the charge that he was taking unilateral decisions, Chirag had called for clarification but quickly backed out after Election Commission released a statement to suggest that decisions were unanimous.

End of Article

title: Bypolls win shows deep connect with people: PM Modi

title: Amid Form 7 bulk filing row, Election Commission limits it to 10 per elector
content: EC capped the maximum number of applications that may be filed by an individual elector during the claims and objections period of special and summary revisions . the ceilings follow Congress flagging bulk filings across many constituencies in Karnataka . a single BJP worker allegedly submitted 7,561 Form 7 applications .
